cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic sine of -2.5
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as -1.647231146. Independently verified in Python: math.asinh(-2.5) = -1.6472311463710958 = ln(-2.5 + sqrt(7.25)) -> -1.647231146 at 9 dp

cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic sine of 10
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 2.99822295. Independently verified in Python: math.asinh(10) = 2.99822295029797 = ln(10 + sqrt(101)) -> 2.99822295 at 8 dp

cases.description: The inverse hyperbolic sine of zero, which the documented identity ASINH(SINH(x)) = x forces to be zero
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "ASINH(SINH(number)) equals number" and sinh(0) = 0, so asinh(0) = 0 exactly. Unlike ACOSH, the documented domain here is "any real number", so zero is inside it
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the ACOT page states it explicitly for this inverse-hyperbolic family
